It goes LOW at t = 0.8 ms and back HIGH at t = 3 ms.
It goes LOW at t = 0.8 ms and back LOW at t = 1 ms.

pool.q: Same setup with a 2-input NOR gate, the output pulse:
o: goes HIGH at t=0.8ms and LOW at t=1ms
goes LOW at t=0.8ms and HIGH again at t=3ms
goes LOW at t=0.8ms and HIGH again at t=1ms
goes LOW at t=0 and HIGH again at t=3ms
pool.e: NOR goes HIGH only when BOTH inputs are LOW: true only before t = 0 and after t = 3ms; NOR drops LOW as soon as one pulse goes HIGH (t = 0) and rises HIGH again only when both are LOW (after t = 3ms).

A bus that supports the transfer of data in both directions is referred to as:
pool.e: A bus that can carry data both ways is called bidirectional (e.g. ARINC 629, AFDX, MIL-STD-1553); ARINC 429 by contrast is unidirectional only.

pool.q: The main advantage of using a serial bus in an aircraft is:
o: reduction in the size and weight of cabling
there is no need for data conversion
it supports the highest possible data rates
pool.e: A serial bus needs only one or two wire pairs instead of dozens of parallel wires, sharply cutting weight and installation space, matching reason #1 in the lecture slide (fewer wires, lower weight).

pool.q: Which one of the following is used to minimise reflections present in a bus cable:
pool.e: A terminating resistor (e.g. 78Ω at both ends of the ARINC 629 bus, per the lecture slide) absorbs the signal at the end of the cable, preventing reflections that would otherwise cause interference.

pool.q: The data format in an ARINC 429 stub cable consists of:
o: parallel data from the local bus
pool.e: Per Tooley's own answer key, the ARINC 429 stub cable carries "serial analogue doublets": successive pairs of analogue voltage pulses, NOT Manchester-encoded data (easy to confuse, since Manchester is the encoding used by a different bus standard, ARINC 708/573).

pool.q: In order to represent negative data values, BNR data uses:
o: an extra parity bit to indicate the sign
BCD data and a binary sign bit
pool.e: BNR (Binary Number Representation) encodes a signed integer using two's complement across the 19-bit Data field, with bit 29 (the Data field's MSB) acting as the sign bit.

pool.q: The physical bus media specified in ARINC 629 is:
pool.e: ARINC 629 uses shielded twisted pair (STP) cable, physically similar to ARINC 429, but with a very different protocol (2 Mbps, bidirectional, no central bus controller needed).

pool.q: The validity of an ARINC 429 data word is checked by using:
pool.e: The last bit (bit 32) of the 32-bit word is an odd-parity bit: the total count of 1-bits across the whole word is always odd, letting the receiver detect simple single-bit errors.

pool.q: The label field in an ARINC 429 data word consists of:
pool.e: The Label occupies exactly 8 bits (bits 1-8), enough to encode 256 different data types (0-255), e.g. Label 203 = airspeed in the lecture's example label table.

pool.q: The voltages present on an ARINC 429 data bus cable are:
pool.e: Each conductor (A or B) carries +5V, 0V or -5V with respect to ground; only the DIFFERENTIAL voltage between the two wires reaches ±10V. The question asks about the voltage ON THE CABLE (each wire), so the answer is ±5V.

pool.q: The maximum bit rate supported by ARINC 429 is:
pool.e: ARINC 429 has two speeds: low speed 12.5 kbps (most common) and high speed 100 kbps, which is the MAXIMUM rate supported.

pool.q: An ARINC 429 NULL state is represented by:
pool.e: NULL (no data present) corresponds to both wires A and B sitting at 0V, distinct from bit 1 (A=+5V, B=-5V) and bit 0 (A=-5V, B=+5V).

pool.q: The maximum data rate supported by MIL-STD-1553 is:
pool.e: MIL-STD-1553B supports 1 Mbps, faster than ARINC 429 (max 100 kbps) but slower than ARINC 629 (2 Mbps) and AFDX (100 Mbps).

pool.q: A bus that is self-clocking is referred to as:
pool.e: ARINC 429's BPRZ encoding always has a transition in the middle of every bit (return to 0V), so the receiver can recover timing from the signal itself with no separate clock wire: this is the self-clocking property.

pool.q: The physical bus media specified in MIL-STD-1773B is:
pool.e: MIL-STD-1773B is the fibre-optic implementation of MIL-STD-1553B, giving much greater immunity to high-intensity radiated electromagnetic fields (HIRF) than copper cable.

pool.q: The length of an ARINC 429 word is:
pool.e: An ARINC 429 word is always 32 bits long: Label(8)+SDI(2)+Data(19)+SSM(2)+Parity(1) = 32.

pool.q: ARINC 573 is designed for use with:
pool.e: ARINC 573 is the standard for Flight Data Recorders (FDR), using 12-bit Harvard Bi-Phase encoding; ARINC 717 later superseded ARINC 573.

pool.q: The maximum data rate supported by the FDDI bus is:
pool.e: FDDI (Fibre Distributed Data Interface), developed by Boeing for the 777, supports 100 Mbps over a dual token-ring topology.

pool.q: A USB 3.0 cable contains:
pool.e: USB 3.0 has the 2.0 twisted pair D+/D- plus two more twisted pairs.

pool.q: Which of the following is NOT a USB speed classification?
pool.e: USB has four speed classes: low, full, high, super; there is no "intermediate".
pool.s: Floyd Ch.13 · Self-Test #28 (printed key (b), site uses (d))

pool.q: The bus typically used to connect systems in an automobile is the:
pool.e: CAN (controller area network).

pool.q: Properties that define a bus include:
o: all of these: connector type, cable length and type, data rate and encoding
pool.e: Floyd Self-Test question 23: answer (d) all of these.

pool.q: ARINC 629 supports a data transmission rate of:
pool.e: ARINC 629 reaches 2 Mbps, 20 times faster than ARINC 429's top speed (100 kbps), matching the figures in the lecture slide.
pool.s: Added · generated from the content of module 05 (slide number not yet attached)

pool.q: The channel access mechanism used by ARINC 629 is:
pool.e: ARINC 629 uses TDMA: each LRU is assigned one or more fixed time slots within a Major Frame to transmit, avoiding data collisions without needing a central bus controller.
pool.s: Added · generated from the content of module 05 (slide number not yet attached)

pool.q: AFDX (ARINC 664) achieves a maximum transmission rate of:
pool.e: AFDX is 100 Mbps switched full-duplex Ethernet, using the Virtual Link (VL) mechanism to guarantee deterministic bandwidth for each data flow.
pool.s: Added · generated from the content of module 05 (slide number not yet attached)

pool.q: In AFDX, the mechanism that guarantees each data flow its own bandwidth, preventing other flows from consuming it, is called:
pool.e: Each Virtual Link has its own bandwidth, frame size and transmission period (BAG); the AFDX switch isolates VLs from each other so that one faulty flow cannot congest the whole network.
pool.s: Added · generated from the content of module 05 (slide number not yet attached)

pool.q: A central bus controller is a required component of which of the following bus standards?
pool.e: MIL-STD-1553B uses a command-response architecture with one Bus Controller (BC) managing up to 31 Remote Terminals (RT); ARINC 629, by contrast, was designed to need NO central bus controller (avoiding a single point of failure).
pool.s: Added · generated from the content of module 05 (slide number not yet attached)

pool.q: The SSM field in an ARINC 429 data word is used to:
o: report data status (valid, failure, test mode...)
specify which device receives the data
identify the type of data being transmitted
pool.e: SSM (Sign/Status Matrix, 2 bits) reports one of 4 context-dependent data states, e.g. for BNR: 00=Failure Warning, 01=No Computed Data, 10=Functional Test, 11=Normal Operation.
pool.s: Added · generated from the content of module 05 (slide number not yet attached)

pool.q: If a 32-bit ARINC 429 word is transmitted at 100 kbps, the time to transmit one word is:
pool.e: t = N/R = 32 bits / 100,000 bit/s = 0.00032 s = 0.32 ms, matching the Data Rate and Bit Timing table in the lecture slide.
pool.s: Added · generated from the content of module 05 (slide number not yet attached)

pool.q: With 6 sensors each sending its own data to 4 displays, how many wires does point-to-point need, and how many does a shared bus need (1 wire per device)?
pool.e: Point-to-point: 6 × 4 = 24; shared bus: 6 + 4 = 10.

pool.q: How many receivers can one ARINC 429 transmitter feed at most?
pool.e: ARINC 429 is a one-way bus: 1 transmitter feeds at most 20 receivers.

pool.q: Why does an LRU such as the ADIRU have both Tx and Rx pins although ARINC 429 is a one-way bus?
o: Because each wire of one 429 channel runs in a different direction
Because the ADIRU reverses the bus direction when needed
Because each 429 channel carries one direction, so sending and receiving are separate channels
pool.e: Two-way exchange needs two separate one-way channels.

pool.q: The differential voltage between wires A and B of ARINC 429 when sending a 1 is:
pool.e: Bit 1: A = +5 V, B = -5 V so A - B = +10 V.

pool.q: Why does BPRZ coding let the receiver do without a separate clock line?
o: Because every bit has a rising and a falling edge, so there is always a reference to count timing
Because BPRZ runs faster than the receiver's clock
Because BPRZ sends the clock on a hidden second wire pair
pool.e: The transition in every bit lets timing be recovered (self-clocking).

pool.q: Which bit is the Parity field of an ARINC 429 word, and what kind of parity is it?
pool.e: Parity is bit 32 (sent last), odd parity.

pool.q: What is the 2-bit SDI field of an ARINC 429 word used for?
o: Reporting whether the data is valid or failed
Distinguishing the source or destination further within the same Label
pool.e: The SDI (Source/Destination Identifier) extends how many channels one Label can tell apart.

pool.q: The BCD encoding of an airspeed of 250 kt, digit by digit 2, 5, 0, is:
In BNR Data format, which bit is the sign bit?
o: Bit 29, the highest bit of the Data field
Bit 11, the lowest bit of the Data field
pool.e: The Data field occupies bits 11 to 29; bit 29 is the MSB and the sign bit of the two's-complement number.

pool.q: How many bits does an ARINC 629 frame have and which fields?
o: 32 bits: Label 8, SDI 2, Data 19, SSM 2, Parity 1
52 bits: Sync 8, Data 32, SDI 2, Label 8, SSM 2
pool.e: 8 + 32 + 2 + 8 + 2 = 52 bits; 32 bits with Parity is ARINC 429.

pool.q: In ARINC 629, how long is a Major Frame and how many slots does it have (per the lecture)?
o: 2 ms with 16 slots of 125 µs each
16 ms with 125 slots of 128 µs each
2 ms with 125 slots of 16 µs each

pool.q: In AFDX, what is the BAG (Bandwidth Allocation Gap)?
o: The minimum time between two consecutive frames of a Virtual Link
The maximum size of an Ethernet frame
The number of switches between two devices
pool.e: The BAG sets a VL's minimum period, which is how bandwidth is guaranteed.

pool.q: A FADEC must send small amounts of engine data with very high reliability in a noisy environment. Which of the four standards fits best?
o: MIL-STD-1553 (or ARINC 717), the dedicated bus for engines
pool.e: The lecture assigns FADEC ↔ engine to MIL-STD-1553/ARINC 717.

pool.q: How does electromagnetic noise act on a twisted pair and why does a differential signal tolerate it?
o: The twisted pair absorbs the noise completely
Noise acts almost equally on both wires, so the difference A - B barely changes
Noise acts only on wire A
pool.e: Common-mode noise cancels when the two wires are subtracted.
pool.s: Data Buses lecture · relevant part; Tooley 14.6.3

pool.q: In the lecture's A320 diagram, over which bus does the ADIRU send data to the FMGC?
pool.e: Air and inertial data from the ADIRU travels over ARINC 429.

pool.q: Slide 14 of the Data Buses lecture says ARINC 429 uses Manchester Biphase-L coding. Is that right or wrong, and why?
o: Wrong: ARINC 429 uses BPRZ, Manchester belongs to ARINC 708
Right but only at the high speed
pool.e: Two other slides of the same lecture and Tooley both confirm BPRZ.
pool.s: Data Buses lecture · slides 3, 13, 14; Tooley ch.4

pool.q: Two ARINC 429 devices want to exchange data both ways. How many 429 channels are needed at least?
o: 4 channels because each wire is a channel
pool.e: Each channel is one-way so two-way needs two channels.

pool.q: Which ordering lists the four buses by increasing speed?
pool.e: 100 kbps < 1 Mbps < 2 Mbps < 100 Mbps.

pool.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the reasons for using data buses on aircraft?
o: Fewer wires, less weight and space
Increasing the number of wires for more redundancy
pool.e: A bus reduces wire count; redundancy comes from independent buses, not from more wires.

pool.q: An ARINC 429 word uses ODD parity. The first 31 bits contain 17 ones. The parity bit (bit 32) and the total number of ones of the whole word are:
pool.e: The total number of ones must be odd: 17 is odd so the parity bit = 0.
pool.s: Added · Level 3: Odd parity of a 429 word

pool.q: An ARINC 429 word uses ODD parity. The first 31 bits contain 22 ones. The parity bit (bit 32) and the total number of ones of the whole word are:
pool.e: The total number of ones must be odd: 22 is even so the parity bit = 1.

pool.q: A multifunction display (MFD) can be:
o: configured for more than one type of information
used only for basic flight information
set to display information from the standby magnetic compass
pool.e: An MFD is a configurable display: weather radar, navigation map, checklists, or a substitute for the PFD/ND if either fails (Tooley 1.1.5.6).

pool.q: Which standby instruments are driven from the aircraft's pitot-static system:
o: Airspeed indicator, vertical speed indicator and magnetic compass
Airspeed indicator, altimeter and vertical speed indicator
Airspeed indicator, altimeter and angle-of-attack indicator
pool.e: The three air data instruments (ASI, altimeter, VSI) use static and pitot pressure. The magnetic compass is an independent magnetic device and needs no pitot-static supply.

pool.q: Static pressure is fed:
o: only to the airspeed indicator and vertical speed indicator
to the airspeed indicator as well as the altimeter and vertical speed indicator
pool.e: Static pressure goes to all three instruments; only the ASI additionally receives ram (pitot) pressure to compare against (Figure 1.11).

pool.q: The horizontal situation indicator (HSI) uses information derived from:
pool.e: The HSI combines compass and radio navigation (VOR) information to show the horizontal situation (Tooley Table 1.1).

pool.q: The term 'glass cockpit' refers to:
o: the use of toughened glass windows
the use of a transparent partition between the flight deck and passenger cabin
the use of LCD and CRT displays
pool.e: A "glass cockpit" uses CRT and LCD screens in place of electromechanical dials (Tooley section 1.1).

pool.q: Basic air data instruments are:
o: airspeed indicator, vertical speed indicator and artificial horizon
airspeed indicator, altimeter and magnetic compass
airspeed indicator, altimeter and vertical speed indicator
pool.e: The three pitot-static driven instruments are called air data instruments: ASI, altimeter, VSI.

pool.q: Three airborne parameters that can be used to assess aircraft position are:
pool.e: Heading, airspeed and height are the basic quantities that fix the aircraft's position; weight is not a position parameter.

pool.q: The instrument shown in Figure 1.27 is the:
pool.e: The dial is marked "IAS KNOTS" with a 60 to 400 scale: it is an airspeed indicator (ASI).

pool.q: Engine parameters such as turbine speed are displayed on:
pool.e: ECAM (Airbus) and EICAS (Boeing) show engine parameters; the EADI and EHSI are flight and navigation displays.

pool.q: The aircraft slip indicator is found in the:
pool.e: The EADI contains the slip indicator (together with the attitude display, command bars, glide slope pointer, localiser indicator).

pool.q: Where is the 'rising runway':
pool.e: The symbolic runway (rising runway) is the localiser indicator on the EADI; it appears once the pilot has acquired the glide slope.

pool.q: Under visual flight rules (VFR) the pilot's most important source of information concerning the aircraft's position and attitude is:
o: the altimeter and vertical speed indicators
the airspeed indicator and the magnetic compass
the view out of the cockpit window
pool.e: Tooley section 1.1: under VFR the most important source of information is the view out of the cockpit window.

pool.q: The EFIS fitted to a large aircraft usually consists of:
o: separate primary flight and navigation displays
a primary display with several standby instruments
pool.e: The EFIS consists of a PFD (or EADI) and an ND (or EHSI), duplicated for the captain and first officer (Tooley 1.1.5).

pool.q: The instrument shown in Figure 1.28 is the:
pool.e: The figure shows "HDG", VOR, WPT, distance and a rotating compass: it is the EHSI (horizontal situation).

pool.q: The instrument shown in Figure 1.29 is the:
pool.e: The figure has the attitude horizon (±10, ±20 pitch scale), command bars, glide slope, LAND 3 and VNAV modes: it is the EADI.

pool.q: In a basic 'T' configuration of instruments:
o: the ASI appears on the left and the altimeter appears on the right
the ADI appears on the left and the HSI appears on the right
the ADI appears on the left and the ASI appears on the right
pool.e: The T: ASI left, ADI top centre, altimeter right, HSI below the ADI (Tooley Figure 1.23).

pool.q: The flight director system receives information:
o: only from the attitude gyro and altimeter
pool.e: The flight director takes data from the attitude gyro, the VOR/localiser/glide slope receiver, the radar altimeter, the compass system and barometric sensors (Tooley 1.1.4).

pool.q: EICAS provides the following information:
pool.e: EICAS shows engine parameters, crew alerts and system pages (electrical, hydraulic, fuel...); navigation data belongs to the ND.

pool.q: The two sets of flight regulations that a pilot may fly by are:
pool.e: VFR (visual flight rules) and IFR (instrument flight rules).

pool.q: A major advantage of EFIS is a reduction in:
o: moving parts present in the flight deck
pool.e: EFIS replaces electromechanical dials with static screens, cutting moving parts. EFIS actually increases EMI (Tooley section 15.2), it does not reduce it.

pool.q: The term 'artificial horizon' is sometimes used to describe the indication produced by:
pool.e: The attitude indicator shows the aircraft relative to the horizon, hence the name artificial horizon (Tooley Table 1.1).

pool.q: Typical displays on an EHSI are:
pool.e: The EHSI shows heading, track, VOR/DME/ILS/ADF, wind and range (Tooley 1.1.3.2). Altitude and vertical speed belong to the PFD.

pool.q: In a basic 'T' configuration of instruments:
o: the ADI appears at the top and the HSI appears at the bottom
the ASI appears at the top and the ADI appears at the bottom
the HSI appears at the top and the ASI appears at the bottom
pool.e: The top bar of the T holds ASI, ADI, altimeter; the ADI is top centre and the HSI sits directly below it.

pool.q: Operational faults in FMS can be detected by:
o: automatically comparing outputs on a continuous basis
routine maintenance inspection of the aircraft
pool.e: The two FMSs (captain and first officer) compare indications and outputs continuously to detect faults (Tooley 1.1.8).

pool.q: The display marked X in Figure 1.30 is the:
pool.e: X points at the unit on the centre pedestal between the two pilot seats: the FMS CDU.

pool.q: The display marked Y in Figure 1.31 is the:
pool.e: Y points at the large screen directly in front of the captain: the primary flight display (PFD).

pool.q: The upper ECAM display provides:
pool.e: The upper ECAM screen (E/WD) shows engine parameters and warnings; the lower one shows system pages (Tooley 1.1.6).

pool.q: The peak wavelength of light emitted from a red LED is typically:
pool.e: Tooley Table 11.1 gives 635 nm for red LEDs (the miniature type 690 nm). 475 nm is blue, 525 nm is green.

pool.q: The spectral response of the human eye peaks at around:
pool.e: The eye is most sensitive near 550 nm (green light), Figure 11.12; the lecture gives a 555 nm peak.

pool.q: Adjacent phosphors of blue and green are illuminated on the screen of a CRT. The resultant colour produced will be:
pool.e: Green + blue = cyan; red + green = yellow; red + blue = magenta; all three = white (Figure 11.9).

pool.q: The human eye is most sensitive to:
pool.e: The correct answer is green (peak near 550 nm, consistent with question 2, Figure 11.12 and lecture slide 6). Note: the answer key printed in Tooley (Appendix 3, A.11) gives question 4 as (a), which contradicts the chapter's own question 2, so it is treated as a printing error; the site uses (c).
pool.s: Tooley Ch.11 Q4 (printed key says (a), site uses (c): see explanation)

pool.q: A seven-segment LED display has segments a, b, c, d and g illuminated. The character displayed will be:
pool.e: Segments a, b, c, d, g form a 3. A 2 needs e instead of c; a 5 needs f instead of b. (Checked in the notebook.)

pool.q: The BCD input to a seven-segment display decoder is 1001. The digit displayed will be:
pool.e: 1001₂ = 9 (BCD). The digit 8 has code 1000.

pool.q: The potential at the grid of a CRT is:
o: negative with respect to the cathode
positive with respect to the cathode
pool.e: The grid is held negative with respect to the cathode to repel electrons, which controls brightness (Tooley 11.1.1).

pool.q: The function of the final anode of a CRT is:
o: controlling the brightness of the display
pool.e: The final anode sits at a very high positive potential (several kilovolts) to accelerate the beam; deflection is by X/Y plates or coils, brightness by the grid.

pool.q: Electromagnetic deflection of a CRT uses:
o: coils around the neck of the CRT
X- and Y-plates inside the CRT
pool.e: Electromagnetic deflection uses two sets of coils placed externally around the neck of the tube; X and Y plates inside are electrostatic deflection.

pool.q: The three beams in a colour CRT are associated with the colours:
pool.e: The three electron guns correspond to the red, green and blue phosphors (RGB).

pool.q: When compared with CRT displays, AMLCD displays have:
pool.e: The main AMLCD advantages are weight, power, volume and reliability (Tooley, chapter 11 introduction).

pool.q: The final anode of a CRT display requires:
pool.e: The final anode needs a steady high positive potential (several kilovolts DC) to accelerate the beam.

pool.q: The deflecting waveform supplied to the plates of an electrostatic CRT will be:
pool.e: Raster scanning uses ramp (sawtooth) waveforms at two different frequencies on the X and Y plates.

pool.q: The typical value of maximum forward current for an LED indicator is:
pool.e: Table 11.1: maximum forward current is 30 to 40 mA, i.e. 0.03 to 0.04 A.

pool.q: The patterns required to display alphanumeric characters in a CRT controller are stored in:
pool.e: Character shapes are fixed, so they live in a character generator ROM (Figure 11.11).

pool.q: When compared with passive matrix LCDs, AMLCDs are:
pool.e: Passive matrices respond slowly and are less sharp; the AMLCD uses a TFT per cell, so it is faster and sharper (Tooley 11.3.2, 11.3.3).

pool.q: The standard for ACARS is defined in:
pool.e: ACARS was originally specified in ARINC 597 and revised as ARINC 724B (Tooley 15.1).

pool.q: Engine parameters are displayed on:
pool.e: ECAM (Airbus) shows engine and system parameters; the EHSI is a navigation display and the CDU is the FMS data entry unit.

pool.q: The left and right cockpit displays:
o: are supplied from the same symbol generator
will only be supplied from the same symbol generator when all other symbol generators have failed
are supplied from separate symbol generators at all times
pool.e: The left generator feeds the captain's displays, the right one the first officer's, the centre one is a backup; only when the others have failed do both sides share one generator (Tooley 15.2.2).

pool.q: On a flight deck EFIS system, if all of the displays were missing information from a particular source, the most likely cause would be:
o: the display controller and symbol generator
the sensor, input bus or display controller
pool.e: A fault common to every display lies upstream of all of them: the source sensor, the input bus or the display controller; not one individual symbol generator.

pool.q: A central maintenance computer provides:
o: ground and BITE testing using a portable control panel
display of system warnings and cautions
ground and in-flight monitoring and testing
pool.e: The CMC collects fault and status data from the LRUs continuously, in flight and on the ground; displaying warnings is the job of the FWC/ECAM.

pool.q: The sweep voltage waveform used on an electromagnetic CRT is:
pool.e: Because the deflection coils have resistance, the scan voltage must be trapezoidal rather than the straight sawtooth of an electrostatic CRT (Tooley 15.2.2).

pool.q: In an EFIS with three symbol generators, what is the purpose of the third symbol generator?
o: comparison with the pilot's symbol generator
pool.e: The centre generator is a backup that can replace the left or right one on failure (Tooley 15.2.2).

pool.q: The ACARS system uses channels in the:
pool.e: ACARS uses the VHF band 129 to 137 MHz (Tooley 15.1, Table 15.1).

pool.q: If one EICAS CRT fails:
o: the FMS CDU will display the failed CRT data
the standby CRT will automatically take over
the remaining CRT will display primary EICAS data
pool.e: The remaining screen displays the primary EICAS data; secondary pages are called up from the control panel when needed.

pool.q: A method used in modern aircraft for reporting in-flight faults to an engineering and monitoring ground station is:
pool.e: ACARS sends performance, fault and maintenance data from the aircraft to the airline over the VHF link.

pool.q: Would you select a decoder/driver with active-HIGH or active-LOW outputs to drive a common-cathode 7-segment LED display?
pool.e: A common-cathode display lights a segment when its anode is driven HIGH, so active-HIGH outputs are needed. The 74HC47 has active-LOW outputs, so it suits common-anode displays (Floyd p.339).
pool.s: Floyd Ch.6 · Section 6-5 Checkup #3 (p.341; answer p.384)

pool.q: In the 7-segment display multiplexing system of Figure 6-49, which IC enables the two displays alternately?
pool.e: The 74HC139 (a decoder) enables digit A and digit B in turn; the 74HC157 selects the BCD code; the 74HC47 decodes to 7 segments.
pool.s: Floyd Ch.6 · Section 6-8 Checkup #4(c) (p.356; answer p.384)

pool.q: In the same system (Figure 6-49), what does the 74HC157 do?
o: Multiplexes the two BCD codes to the 7-segment decoder
Decodes the BCD to energise the display
pool.e: The 74HC157 is a 4-bit data selector (multiplexer): the select line LOW passes the LSD code, HIGH passes the MSD code.
pool.s: Floyd Ch.6 · Section 6-8 Checkup #4(a) (p.356; answer p.384)

pool.q: With the 74HC47, when the LT (lamp test) input is LOW and BI/RBO is HIGH:
pool.e: Lamp test turns on all seven segments to verify that none is burned out (Floyd p.339).

pool.q: Why does the 7-segment display use lowercase b and d instead of capital B and D?
o: Capital letters do not exist in hexadecimal
A capital B would look like an 8 and a capital D like a 0
pool.e: Floyd p.244: the letter b is lowercase because a capital B would be the same as the digit 8; similarly a capital D would look like 0.
pool.s: Floyd Ch.4 · Applied Logic: Seven-Segment Display (p.244)

pool.q: Which statement correctly compares LED and LCD 7-segment displays?
o: Both emit light on their own
An LCD can be seen in the dark, an LED cannot
An LED can be seen in the dark, an LCD cannot
pool.e: Each LED segment is a light-emitting diode, so it makes its own light. An LCD works by polarising light; an activated segment does not reflect light and appears black, so it cannot be seen in the dark (Floyd p.244).
pool.s: Floyd Ch.4 · Applied Logic: Seven-Segment Display (p.244)

pool.q: According to Floyd Table 4-14, which segments form the letter C?
pool.e: Table 4-14: C = a, d, e, f. (b: c,d,e,f,g; d: b,c,d,e,g; E: a,d,e,f,g; A: a,b,c,e,f,g.)

pool.q: To absorb switching spikes on the VCC and ground of a digital board, about what capacitor does Floyd recommend for the whole board?
o: About 1 µF from VCC to ground
About 1000 µF between two signal pins
About 1 nF in series with VCC
pool.e: Floyd 6-11: 1 µF for the board and 0.022 to 0.1 µF distributed.

pool.q: With a visual acuity of 1 arcminute (2.91×10⁻⁴ rad), the smallest size the eye can still resolve at 10 m is:

pool.s: Added · generated from the content of module 06 (slide number not yet attached)

pool.e: The DMC generates the display information; the FWC generates warnings; the SDAC collects system data and passes it to the DMCs.

pool.q: On a PFD the glide slope pointer and localiser indicator are both centred. Where is the pilot relative to the ILS approach path?

Below the glide path but on the centreline
Above the glide path and left of the centreline

pool.q: On the ND in ROSE NAV mode, where is the aircraft shown and how does the compass behave?

The aircraft is fixed at the centre and the compass rotates with heading
The aircraft moves over a fixed north-up map

pool.q: On the ECAM E/WD, the typical range of EPR and its meaning are:

About 0 to 100; percentage of fan speed
pool.e: EPR = engine pressure ratio, typically about 1.0 to 1.6.

pool.q: On the ECAM PRESS page, what does "CAB ALT" indicate?

pool.e: CAB ALT is the simulated cabin altitude (ft) maintained by the pressurisation system.

pool.q: On the ECAM ELEC page, if GEN 1 is lost, which bus loses its direct supply from it?

pool.e: GEN 1 feeds AC 1; TR 1 rectifies AC 1 into DC 1.

pool.q: The normal pressure of the three hydraulic systems GREEN, BLUE, YELLOW on the A320 per the lecture is:
pool.e: 3000 psi is the typical working pressure of an aircraft hydraulic system.

pool.q: In the lecture's FUEL page example, with the pumps OFF the displayed FOB is 12,707 kg. This number is:
o: The sum of the five tanks: 686 + 2742 + 5852 + 2741 + 686
Only the centre tank 5852 plus the two inner tanks
Fuel used plus remaining fuel of one engine
pool.e: FOB (fuel on board) is the total fuel in all tanks.

pool.q: Which statement is right about the link between display resolution and human visual acuity at the viewing distance?
o: The larger the pixel the less the eye sees it
If the pixel is smaller than h = D·θ the eye can no longer see individual pixels
Viewing distance does not affect seeing pixels
pool.e: The smallest size the eye resolves is proportional to distance D.

pool.q: About how many megapixels is HD 1280×720?
Which liquid crystal alignment gives high contrast and deep blacks, used in high-end cockpits?
pool.e: Slide 4: MVA gives high contrast and deep blacks; IPS a wide viewing angle; TN is cheap but narrow.

A thin-film transistor (TFT) acting as a switch
pool.e: The TFT takes the data-line voltage when the gate line selects the row and holds it with a capacitor.

pool.q: Why is a third (backup) symbol generator useful in an EFIS?

Because it doubles the screen drawing speed
Because it can replace the left or right one if either fails
pool.e: The centre one is the third-level backup for the two main ones.

pool.q: The aircraft CMC has two identical units. What are their roles?
o: Both process in parallel to increase speed
One for the engines and one for the cabin
CMC 1 is active and CMC 2 is standby
pool.e: Lecture slide 19: CMC1 active, CMC2 standby.

pool.q: The placard "Use of Wi-Fi devices on the flight deck prohibited while engines operating for purpose of flight" is which kind of EMC measure?
o: Reducing the coupling path with shielded cable
Reducing the noise source by operating procedure
pool.e: Banning Wi-Fi removes the interfering transmitter.

minor injuries to passengers or crew

pool.q: With the BCD code 0111 and EVEN parity, the parity bit is:
pool.e: 0111 has three 1s (odd), so the even parity bit must be 1 to make four (even). Matches Table 2-8 (P = 1 for 0111).

pool.q: What can a parity bit detect?
o: A single bit error (or an odd number of errors) in the group
Any error whatsoever occurring in the group
Two bit errors within the same group
pool.e: Floyd: parity detects a single bit error (or any odd number of errors) but cannot check for two errors in one group.

pool.q: In Floyd's CRC example with D = 11010011 and G = 1010, the transmitted code is:
pool.e: Append four zeros, divide modulo-2 by 1010 to get remainder 0100; replacing the four zeros with 0100 gives 110100110100. Dividing again by 1010 leaves 0 (checked in code in the notebook).

pool.q: The receiver divides the received data by the generator code G and finds a NON-ZERO remainder. This means:
o: Append zeros and divide once more
There is no error, the data is accepted
A transmission error is detected, request retransmission
pool.e: Step 7 of Floyd's CRC process: a non-zero remainder means an error has been detected and the receiver requests retransmission.

pool.q: According to Floyd, how is the checksum in the ROM test example produced?
o: Summing each column of bits and discarding carries (XOR of each column)
Dividing the ROM contents by a fixed generator code
Multiplying all the words and keeping the low 8 bits
pool.e: Floyd 11-11: the checksum is the sum of each column of data bits discarding the carries, i.e. the XOR sum of each column (Figure 11-74).
pool.s: Floyd Ch.11 · section 11-11, ROM checksum test

pool.q: Which odd-parity code is in error? (a) 1011 (b) 1110 (c) 0101 (d) 1000
pool.e: Odd parity: the number of 1s must be odd; 0101 has two 1s (even) so it is in error.

pool.q: Which even-parity code is in error? (a) 11000110 (b) 00101000 (c) 10101010 (d) 11111011
pool.e: 11111011 has seven 1s (odd), violating even parity.

pool.q: Add an even parity bit to the end of the code 1010100 (three 1s). The resulting code is:
pool.e: Three 1s is odd so the even parity bit is 1: 10101001.

pool.q: In Floyd's modulo-2 operation, what is 1 + 1?
pool.e: Modulo-2 is binary addition with the carry discarded, which is the XOR gate (Table 2-9).
pool.s: Floyd Ch.2 · Section 2-12 Checkup #5 and Table 2-9

pool.q: In Floyd Example 2-42 the received data is 100100110100 (one bit in error) with generator G = 1010. The remainder of the division is:
pool.e: Dividing modulo-2 by 1010 gives remainder 0100, non-zero.

pool.q: At which level are flight control and navigation software certified, and why?

Level C, because failure would only make passengers uncomfortable and not affect the flight
Level E, because the pilots can always take over and fly by hand without any automation

A one-way 100 kbps serial bus standard used for basic avionics in the electronics bay

System to high-level requirements, and test cases to test procedures

Quarantine it and hold it pending the supplier's integrity or version checks

pool.q: Two bytes of a file are swapped. A simple additive checksum will:
o: always change, so the error is always detected
stay the same, so the error is not detected
always be 0, so the file is reported valid

insert the software disk into the PDL drive within 5 minutes
switch on the 115 V AC (400 Hz) supply to the EEC to start loading

o: A standard for the aircraft's 115 V 400 Hz supply
A standard for optical fibre on aircraft
A standard for the safety of software in aircraft, setting design assurance levels and used by the FAA and EASA as certification guidance

A technician's on-site signature is enough
The operator may change it provided it is logged

Software the certificate holder declares may be modified within certification constraints; for example ACMS, IFE
A navigation database; for example the FMC

Approved and validated components the operator may activate within boundaries defined by the certificate holder

As ordinary data needing no records
Like LSAP code: its own unique part number and release documentation

Distribution over a network with no intermediate media

The version of the FLS and DFLD currently installed

An LSAP such as an EEC, DFDAU, APU ECU, FGC or IMA unit

28 V DC to the loader and 115 V AC (400 Hz) to the EEC

pool.q: Supply-borne noise can be eliminated by means of:

pool.e: Tooley 15.8: the RA pitch command has the highest priority; without altitude data from the target an RA will not occur.

pool.q: If the intruder provides no altitude data, TCAS assumes its relative altitude is within:
pool.e: Tooley 15.8.

pool.q: TCAS needs the landing-gear position sensors because:
o: the extended gear disturbs the lower directional antenna, so detection of traffic below must be inhibited
the extended gear switches off the transponder
the extended gear makes the aircraft heavier
pool.e: Tooley 15.8 also lists the IRS, the radio altimeter and the GPWS (GPWS overrides TCAS).

pool.q: Automatic test equipment (ATE) is:
o: a self-test built into the aircraft
a dedicated ground test instrument that runs many tests and functional checks on an LRU or printed circuit card
pool.e: ATE is expensive so it is usually used only by OEMs and licensed repairers (Tooley 15.9).

pool.q: BITE is primarily:
o: a self-test feature built into airborne equipment as an integral fault indicator
a test set kept in the workshop
pool.e: BITE is usually a signal-flow type test (Tooley 15.10).

pool.q: Which of the following is NOT a BITE capability listed by Tooley?
pool.e: Tooley's list covers real-time monitoring, continuous display, failure isolation, status verification, alarms, quantitative displays and percentage of deterioration.

pool.q: After the flight crew records an ECAM failure message, maintenance staff can follow it up using:
o: the test facilities on the cockpit maintenance panel and the BITE on each computer
pool.e: Tooley 15.10.

pool.q: In a simple ethernet arrangement a host is able to detect whether a bus is idle or busy by means of:
pool.e: That is the CS of CSMA/CD (Tooley 16.4).

pool.q: In an AFDX network the links from each host to the switch are:
pool.e: AFDX is a switched full-duplex network: each link typically has two twisted pairs (Tooley 16.5).

pool.q: Within an AFDX switch a buffer is used:
o: for both received and transmitted data
pool.e: Each received packet is buffered before storage and then copied to the TX buffer(s) (store and forward), so collisions are eliminated (Tooley 16.5).

pool.q: The back-off strategy for a simple ethernet system is based on:
o: re-transmission immediately following the detection of a collision
re-transmission at a random time within a given time interval
pool.e: The random interval doubles after each collision: binary exponential back-off (Tooley 16.4).

pool.q: What is the maximum BAG for a VL that supplies messages at a rate of 400 per second:
pool.e: The BAG frequency must be at least 400 Hz: a 2 ms BAG is 500 Hz while 4 ms is only 250 Hz (Tooley 16.8, Table 16.1).
pool.s: Tooley Ch.16 · Q5 (printed key (b), correct (a); A.16, p.381)

pool.q: What is the maximum bit-rate that can be supported by an AFDX virtual link in which the maximum frame length is 256 bytes and the BAG is 128 ms:
pool.e: $256\times8\times1000/128=16{,}000$ bits per second.

pool.q: Allowable bandwidth allocation gaps in AFDX can range from:
Within an AFDX network, the ethernet frames associated with a particular VL can originate at:
o: one, and only one, end system
each end system present in the network
pool.e: The frame of a VL must originate at one, and only one, end system (Tooley 16.7).

pool.q: Within the transmit protocol stack the ethernet header is added by the:
pool.e: The message passes UDP, then IP, then the link layer; the link layer builds the ethernet frame last (Tooley 16.9).
pool.s: Tooley Ch.16 · Q9 (printed key (b), correct (c); A.16, p.381)

pool.q: Within the AFDX frame the FCS appears:
o: after the IP address and before the message field
pool.e: Order: payload, padding if needed, SN, then the FCS at the end of the frame (Tooley 16.9, Figure 16.7).

pool.q: The order in which a message is passed through the AFDX transmit protocol stack is:
o: UDP transport layer, IP network layer, link layer
IP network layer, UDP transport layer, link layer
link layer, IP network layer, UDP transport layer
pool.e: Reception is the reverse (Tooley 16.9).

pool.q: The fundamental network architecture used by an AFDX network is:
pool.e: Several avionic systems connect to one or more central switches (Tooley 16.5).

pool.q: In an AFDX network, the length of the FCS is:
pool.e: The FCS is 4 bytes, a CRC computed over the whole frame (Tooley 16.9).

pool.q: An AFDX frame sequence number can take a value between:
pool.e: The SN starts at 0 at start-up, increments to 255 and then wraps to 1 (Tooley 16.9).

pool.q: In an AFDX network the length of the UDP header is:
pool.e: The common header 6 + 6 + 2 + 20 + 8 bytes (MAC destination, source, Type, IP, UDP) gives exactly 64 bytes for the smallest frame.

pool.q: The order of successive frames received by an end system can be checked using:
pool.e: Integrity checking uses the SNs to make sure frames arrive in order (Tooley 16.9).

pool.q: In an IMA-based aircraft multiple avionics functions are:
o: federated without the need for a centralised computing platform
performed individually by software resident solely within LRU
split into software applications and end systems communicating over shared network resources
pool.e: That is the distributed architecture of IMA (Tooley 18.2).

pool.q: In an IMA-based aircraft, dedicated avionics functions such as fuel management and engine control:
o: can only be supplied by the original aircraft manufacturer
can be obtained from different avionic system suppliers
do not communicate using a shared network resource
pool.e: An open IMA supports multiple-source avionics (Tooley 18.2.1).

pool.q: An ARINC 664/AFDX network is used in an IMA-based aircraft. Compared with a federated avionics system this offers:
o: reduced cabling, reduced aircraft weight and lower operating costs
increased cabling, increased aircraft weight and higher operating costs
reduced cabling, reduced aircraft weight and higher operating costs
pool.e: Less cable weight reduces fuel and operating cost (Tooley 18.1).

pool.q: The software applications developed by avionic system suppliers for an IMA-based aircraft:
o: must only be suitable for use with non-critical avionics functions
must permit hosting on a third-party computer system
must be loaded into individual line replaceable units (LRU)
pool.e: IMA application software is not part of the core operating system and can be validated and certified independently (Tooley 18.4).

pool.q: Which one of the following is an essential prerequisite for the real-time operating system (RTOS) used in an IMA-based aircraft?
o: It must support partitioning and scheduling
It must employ end-to-end data encryption
It must use batch processing techniques
pool.e: The RTOS manages memory partitions and time slices (Tooley 18.4).

pool.q: In an ARINC 664 network:
o: end systems must all be directly connected to the IMA platform
virtual links (VL) are established between the IMA platform and end systems
all data is routed through a central switch within the IMA platform
pool.e: VLs are logical channels sharing the physical links (Tooley 16.7, 18.3).

pool.q: Which one of the following describes the network technology found in the IMA-based aircraft using ARINC 664 technology?
pool.e: Tooley 16.5 and 18.3: a switched backbone of cascaded star form.

pool.q: In an IMA-based aircraft, central processing resources are allocated using:
pool.e: Each application has its own memory partition and time slice (Tooley 18.4).

pool.q: The ARINC 653 standard applies to:
pool.e: ARINC 653 is the leading standard for IMA RTOS (Tooley 18.4).

pool.q: The allocation of resources in a real-time operating system is facilitated by:
pool.e: The application executive (APEX) allocates memory and time to each application (Tooley 18.4).

pool.q: A BAG of 8 ms corresponds to a frequency (maximum frames per second) of:
A BAG of 32 ms corresponds to a frequency (maximum frames per second) of:
A BAG of 128 ms corresponds to a frequency (maximum frames per second) of:
A BAG of 2 ms corresponds to a frequency (maximum frames per second) of:
An avionics port supplies data 100 times a second to a VL. The largest BAG (ms) that can be chosen is:
pool.e: We need $1000/\text{BAG}\ge100$ Hz; of 1, 2, 4, ..., 128 ms the largest that works is 8 ms (125 Hz).

pool.q: An avionics port supplies data 30 times a second to a VL. The largest BAG (ms) that can be chosen is:
pool.e: We need $1000/\text{BAG}\ge30$ Hz; of 1, 2, 4, ..., 128 ms the largest that works is 32 ms (31.25 Hz).

pool.q: An avionics port supplies data 200 times a second to a VL. The largest BAG (ms) that can be chosen is:
pool.e: We need $1000/\text{BAG}\ge200$ Hz; of 1, 2, 4, ..., 128 ms the largest that works is 4 ms (250 Hz).

pool.q: An avionics port supplies data 60 times a second to a VL. The largest BAG (ms) that can be chosen is:
pool.e: We need $1000/\text{BAG}\ge60$ Hz; of 1, 2, 4, ..., 128 ms the largest that works is 16 ms (62.5 Hz).

pool.q: An avionics port supplies data 10 times a second to a VL. The largest BAG (ms) that can be chosen is:
pool.e: We need $1000/\text{BAG}\ge10$ Hz; of 1, 2, 4, ..., 128 ms the largest that works is 64 ms (15.625 Hz).

pool.q: A VL has a maximum frame length of 1518 bytes and a BAG of 4 ms. The maximum bit rate of the VL is:
pool.e: $L_{max}\times8\times1000/\text{BAG}=1518\times8\times1000/4$ = 3.036 Mbit/s.
pool.s: Added · Maximum bit rate of a VL

pool.q: A VL has a maximum frame length of 1518 bytes and a BAG of 1 ms. The maximum bit rate of the VL is:
pool.e: $L_{max}\times8\times1000/\text{BAG}=1518\times8\times1000/1$ = 12.144 Mbit/s.
pool.s: Added · Maximum bit rate of a VL

pool.q: A VL has a maximum frame length of 512 bytes and a BAG of 16 ms. The maximum bit rate of the VL is:
pool.e: $L_{max}\times8\times1000/\text{BAG}=512\times8\times1000/16$ = 256 kbit/s.
pool.s: Added · Maximum bit rate of a VL

pool.q: A VL has a maximum frame length of 64 bytes and a BAG of 2 ms. The maximum bit rate of the VL is:
pool.e: $L_{max}\times8\times1000/\text{BAG}=64\times8\times1000/2$ = 256 kbit/s.
pool.s: Added · Maximum bit rate of a VL

pool.q: A VL has a maximum frame length of 1000 bytes and a BAG of 8 ms. The maximum bit rate of the VL is:
pool.e: $L_{max}\times8\times1000/\text{BAG}=1000\times8\times1000/8$ = 1 Mbit/s.
pool.s: Added · Maximum bit rate of a VL

pool.q: An AFDX frame carries 100 bytes of payload. The frame length (not counting the preamble and the inter-frame gap) is:
An AFDX frame carries 10 bytes of payload. The frame length (not counting the preamble and the inter-frame gap) is:
pool.e: 6 + 6 + 2 + 20 + 8 + 10 + 7 (padding up to 17) + 1 (SN) + 4 (FCS) = 64 bytes.

pool.q: An AFDX frame carries 1471 bytes of payload. The frame length (not counting the preamble and the inter-frame gap) is:
An AFDX frame carries 1 bytes of payload. The frame length (not counting the preamble and the inter-frame gap) is:
pool.e: 6 + 6 + 2 + 20 + 8 + 1 + 16 (padding up to 17) + 1 (SN) + 4 (FCS) = 64 bytes.

pool.q: The time to transmit a 1518-byte frame on a 10 Mbit/s network (the frame itself only) is:
The time to transmit a 1518-byte frame on a 100 Mbit/s network (the frame itself only) is:
The time to transmit a 64-byte frame on a 100 Mbit/s network (the frame itself only) is:
The AFDX inter-frame gap is 12 bytes long. On a 100 Mbit/s network it lasts:
The AFDX inter-frame gap is 12 bytes long. On a 10 Mbit/s network it lasts:
An end system sends successive frames; the frame just sent has sequence number 255. The next sequence number is:
pool.e: The SN increments to 255 and wraps to 1 (not 0; 0 is only used at start-up or reset).

pool.q: After start-up the sequence numbers of frames 1, 2, 3, ... are 0, 1, 2, ... The 257th frame carries the sequence number:
pool.e: Frame 256 has SN 255; frame 257 wraps to 1.

pool.q: In binary exponential back-off the first random interval is T. After collision number 3 the interval for choosing the retransmission time is:
pool.e: It doubles with each collision: $2^{2}T=4T$.

pool.q: In binary exponential back-off the first random interval is T. After collision number 4 the interval for choosing the retransmission time is:
pool.e: It doubles with each collision: $2^{3}T=8T$.

pool.q: In binary exponential back-off the first random interval is T. After collision number 5 the interval for choosing the retransmission time is:
pool.e: It doubles with each collision: $2^{4}T=16T$.

pool.q: ARINC 664 replaces ARINC 429 with about a thousand times the bandwidth (Tooley 18.5). If high-speed ARINC 429 is 100 kbit/s, how many times faster is a 100 Mbit/s AFDX network?
AFDX is an implementation of which ARINC standard, based on which technology?
pool.e: It uses commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) parts to cut cost (Tooley 16.5).

pool.q: AFDX was originally developed for which aircraft, and is now also introduced on which (according to Tooley)?
pool.e: Tooley 16.5.

pool.q: Ethernet's CSMA/CD stands for:
o: continuous send, multiple channel, check data
carrier sense, multiple access, collision detection
pool.e: CS: know whether the bus is idle or busy; MA: many hosts share the bus; CD: detect collisions (Tooley 16.4).

pool.q: The four commonly met LAN topologies are:
pool.e: A bus is effectively a tree with one trunk and no branches (Tooley 16.3).

pool.q: In a star topology two nodes that want to communicate:
o: wait for their turn on a closed ring
transmit on one shared cable and avoid collisions
send a request to the central switching element, which gives them a dedicated path
pool.e: Bus and tree use a multiple-access medium so only one device can transmit at a time (Tooley 16.3).

pool.q: Which of the following is a LAN requirement in Tooley 16.2?
o: a high data rate (e.g. 10 to 100 Mbps) and a range of several hundred metres on low-cost, light cabling
a single central controlling device only
a range of thousands of kilometres
pool.e: A LAN should exhibit minimum reliance on centralised components (Tooley 16.2).

pool.q: Why is standard commercial-grade ethernet not robust enough for aerospace?
o: because it gives no guarantee that data will be transferred within a particular time interval (it is not deterministic)
because it cannot use twisted pair
pool.e: A safety-critical network must be predictable in its maximum delay (Tooley 16.6). AFDX adds QoS, determinism and guaranteed dedicated bandwidth.

pool.q: In AFDX packets are routed by what, unlike a conventional ethernet switch that uses the destination MAC address?
pool.e: The VL ID sits in the last two bytes of the destination MAC address, following a 32-bit constant field (Tooley 16.7, 16.9).

pool.q: Which statement about virtual links (VL) and bandwidth is correct?
o: a VL may have several end systems sending at once
the total bandwidth of the VLs cannot exceed the available bandwidth, and two-way communication needs a complementary VL
pool.e: Sub-VLs depend on VLs but have no guaranteed bandwidth (Tooley 16.7).

pool.q: The preamble in front of an ethernet frame consists of:
o: 7 bytes of alternating 0 and 1 bits followed by a 1-byte SFD
pool.e: The preamble gives the end systems time to synchronise; the SFD signals the start of the actual frame (Tooley 16.9).

pool.q: The Type field of an AFDX frame always has the value 0x0800, which means:
pool.e: Tooley 16.9.

pool.q: The two redundant parallel AFDX networks are called:
o: the main network and a spare used only after failure
pool.e: Network B carries an exact replica; only one valid data stream is needed so reliability improves (Tooley 16.9).

pool.q: What does redundancy management do in AFDX?
o: detects and drops replica frames (copies of frames already received)
switches the switch off when overloaded
pool.e: Integrity checking checks that the SNs are in strict order (Tooley 16.9).

pool.q: What is the core difference between IMA and federated avionics?
o: IMA is for military aircraft only
many applications run on a shared computing platform instead of each system having its own computer
pool.e: IMA is a concept, not a specific set of technologies (Tooley 18.1).

pool.q: The three key elements of IMA are a high-integrity common computing resource, a shared dual-redundant network (ARINC 664/AFDX) and:
o: a distributed architecture: centrally computed software applications and remotely located end systems
pool.e: Tooley 18.2.

pool.q: Which of the following can be hosted centrally on an IMA platform?
o: air conditioning, fuel management, brakes and landing gear
pool.e: Also ice and rain protection, proximity sensing and fire detection (Tooley 18.2).

pool.q: An open IMA differs from a closed IMA in that it:
pool.e: The A380 is semi-open (one hardware cabinet supplier, a shared operating system); the Boeing 777 uses Honeywell's AIMS so it is closed (Tooley 18.2.1).

pool.q: On the Airbus A380 a CPIOM differs from an IOM in that it:
o: a CPIOM provides computing resource hosting avionic applications; an IOM only converts non-AFDX data to AFDX
an IOM runs the most critical applications
a CPIOM is only an antenna
pool.e: Tooley 18.3.1.

pool.q: Each avionic application on an IMA platform lives in:
o: its own reserved memory partition (firewalled) with a dedicated time slice
a memory area shared with every other application
pool.e: The APEX manages partitions, processes, timing and error handling; the standard is ARINC 653 (Tooley 18.4).

pool.q: Why may some critical functions (flight and engine control) stay on dedicated avionics computers in a federated architecture even where IMA exists?
o: because IMA cannot use a network
because not every application has to be moved to the IMA platform
pool.e: Tooley 18.4: the trend is gradual, but critical applications may remain on dedicated computers.

pool.q: The VHDL structural level describes a system as:
o: a list of signal names and logical expressions
a collection of interconnected gates and components
a set of logic signals and levels
pool.e: Tooley 17.2: the structural level describes a system as interconnected gates and components.

pool.q: The input and output signals of a VHDL entity are defined in:
pool.e: The entity declaration gives the name and the PORT list of the component (Tooley 17.2).

pool.q: A VHDL entity comprises an entity declaration followed by:
o: a description of the semiconductor technology used
a truth table for the logic
pool.e: The architecture defines the behaviour of the entity (Tooley 17.3).

pool.q: VHDL allows:
o: both concurrent and sequential signal assignment
pool.e: An HDL must model many parallel processes so it is concurrent, while inside a PROCESS the statements run sequentially (Tooley 17.9).

pool.q: Comments in VHDL code start with:
pool.e: A VHDL comment is "--" to the end of the line.

pool.q: In VHDL the std_logic type is defined:
pool.e: The code uses LIBRARY ieee; USE ieee.std_logic_1164.all; (Tooley 17.8).

pool.q: Which one of the following comes earlier in the development of a VHDL program:
pool.e: The order: conception, coding, compilation, simulation, synthesis, fitting/placement/routing, verification (Tooley 17.4).

pool.q: In VHDL code, signals that have not already been initialised are denoted by the letter:
pool.e: std_logic has nine values: U (uninitialised), X (forcing unknown), 0, 1, Z (high impedance), W, L, H and "-" (don't care).

pool.q: The assignment operator in VHDL is represented by:
pool.e: A signal assignment is written sum <= x XOR y; (Tooley 17.3).

pool.q: When program statements are executed in parallel they are said to be:
pool.e: An HDL needs the characteristics of a concurrent, multi-threaded language (Tooley 17.9).

pool.q: Which one of the following is an example of a VHDL data type:
pool.e: IN and BUFFER are signal modes; Boolean is a data type.

pool.q: When x = 101 and y = 011 the VHDL expression not x and y will evaluate to:
pool.e: NOT has higher precedence than AND: NOT 101 = 010; 010 AND 011 = 010.

pool.q: The internal workings of a VHDL entity:
o: are defined in an external IEEE library
pool.e: The entity is a "wrapper" hiding the internal details (Tooley 17.5, 17.6).

pool.q: In VHDL the sum, s, output of a half adder would be coded as:
pool.e: The sum of a half adder is the XOR of the two inputs; the carry is the AND (Tooley 17.3, Table 17.1).

pool.q: With p = 1010 and q = 0110 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "p AND q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 0010.

pool.q: With p = 1010 and q = 0110 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "NOT p AND q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 0100.

pool.q: With p = 1010 and q = 0110 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "p AND NOT q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 1000.

pool.q: With p = 1010 and q = 0110 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "p AND SLA q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 1000.

pool.q: With p = 1010 and q = 0110 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "NOT p AND ROR q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 0001.

pool.q: With p = 0011 and q = 0100 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "p AND q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 0000.

pool.q: With p = 0011 and q = 0100 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "NOT p OR NOT q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 1111.

pool.q: With p = 0010 and q = 0100 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "SLA p AND NOT q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 0000.

pool.q: With p = 1100 and q = 0101 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "NOT p AND q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 0001.

pool.q: With p = 1100 and q = 0101 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "p XOR q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 1001.

pool.q: With p = 1100 and q = 0101 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "NOT (p AND q)" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 1011.

pool.q: With p = 0110 and q = 1100 (4-bit vectors), the VHDL expression "NOT p AND ROR q" (in Tooley's notation, SLA/ROR shift one place) evaluates to:
pool.e: Precedence (Tooley 17.7): NOT highest, then shift/rotate, then AND/OR/XOR. Result 0000.

pool.q: A half adder with an active-high enable EN has x = 1, y = 1, EN = 1. The pair (sum, carry) is:
pool.e: With EN = 1: sum = x XOR y, carry = x AND y; EN = 0 forces both to 0 (Tooley 17.3, Table 17.2).

pool.q: A half adder with an active-high enable EN has x = 1, y = 0, EN = 1. The pair (sum, carry) is:
pool.e: With EN = 1: sum = x XOR y, carry = x AND y; EN = 0 forces both to 0 (Tooley 17.3, Table 17.2).

pool.q: A half adder with an active-high enable EN has x = 1, y = 1, EN = 0. The pair (sum, carry) is:
pool.e: EN = 0 forces both sum and carry to 0 whatever x and y are (Tooley 17.3, Table 17.2).

pool.q: A half adder with an active-high enable EN has x = 0, y = 0, EN = 1. The pair (sum, carry) is:
pool.e: With EN = 1: sum = x XOR y, carry = x AND y; EN = 0 forces both to 0 (Tooley 17.3, Table 17.2).

pool.q: A half adder built from three standard gates (7408, 7404, 7408), each about 15 ns on the longest path. The total delay at the Sum output is about:
pool.e: $3\times15$ ns = 45 ns (Tooley 17.10).

pool.q: A signal path passes through 4 gates in a row, each with a 15 ns delay. In a VHDL model adding the gate_delay constants the total delay is:
pool.e: $4\times15=60$ ns.

pool.q: A signal path passes through 5 gates in a row, each with a 12 ns delay. In a VHDL model adding the gate_delay constants the total delay is:
pool.e: $5\times12=60$ ns.

pool.q: A signal path passes through 6 gates in a row, each with a 8 ns delay. In a VHDL model adding the gate_delay constants the total delay is:
pool.e: $6\times8=48$ ns.

pool.q: Why are truth tables, logic diagrams and Boolean algebra not enough for very large logic systems?
o: they become cumbersome and error-prone and cannot express propagation delays
pool.e: An HDL gives a formal, unambiguous description that can be simulated (Tooley 17.1).

pool.q: VHDL arose from a request by which body, linked to which kind of circuit?
o: the US Department of Defense, very high-speed integrated circuits (VHSIC)
pool.e: Verilog appeared in 1985 and VHDL (VHSIC HDL) two years later (Tooley 17.1).

pool.q: The two HDLs that dominate advanced digital design tools according to Tooley are:
pool.e: Tooley stresses that VHDL is not a general-purpose programming language like C++ or Pascal (17.9).

pool.q: The entity declaration "half_adder" has inputs x, y and outputs sum, carry. Which part of the declaration lists these signals?
pool.e: PORT(x, y: IN bit; sum, carry: OUT bit); (Tooley 17.2).

pool.q: Which VHDL signal mode is used for a tri-state line that is both input and output (but not at the same time)?
pool.e: Tooley 17.6.

pool.q: The BUFFER mode differs from OUT in that:
o: the output value can also be read and used inside the architecture
pool.e: OUT is only available to external entities (Tooley 17.6).

pool.q: How many different values does std_logic have, and what does "-" mean?
Which stage of the VHDL design flow turns the intermediate code into components of the target technology and, for an ASIC, exports a net list?
pool.e: Tooley 17.4 stage 5.

pool.q: Which gives the seven stages of the VHDL design flow in the right order (Tooley 17.4)?
o: conception, coding, compilation, simulation, synthesis, fitting/placement/routing, verification
conception, compilation, coding, synthesis, simulation, verification, fitting/placement/routing
coding, conception, simulation, compilation, verification, synthesis, fitting/placement/routing
pool.e: Simulation comes before synthesis; verification is last, on the real avionics platform.

pool.q: A VHDL test bench is:
o: separate, event-driven code that defines the signals and clock waveforms applied to the component under simulation
pool.e: Tooley 17.9.

pool.q: What is the most important difference between an HDL and an ordinary procedural programming language?
o: an HDL only runs on mainframes
an HDL must model many parallel processes that can happen at the same instant
pool.e: Tooley 17.9.

wpool.q: Compare the federated and IMA architectures on the four criteria of Tooley (Table 18.1): processing, data interconnection and cabling, application software, suppliers. State five benefits of IMA.
wpool.sol: Federated: many embedded computers dedicated to separate functions; many low and medium speed buses (ARINC 429, 629); software resident on each LRU, physically firewalled; restricted suppliers. IMA: centralised processing on a shared, partitioned platform; a common high-speed switched backbone (ARINC 664/AFDX); logically firewalled software; ideally open source, multiple sources. Benefits: manage many functions at once, lighter cabling (fuel, environment, cost), support for new functions (aircraft condition monitoring), multi-source support (flexibility, faster development), fewer spares and less single-source dependence.

wpool.q: Let p = 1100 and q = 0101 (4-bit vectors). Using the VHDL precedence (NOT > shift/rotate > AND/OR/XOR): (a) p AND q; (b) NOT p AND q; (c) NOT (p AND q); (d) p XOR q; (e) explain why (b) and (c) differ.
wpool.sol: (a) 0100. (b) NOT p = 0011, AND q = 0001. (c) p AND q = 0100, NOT = 1011. (d) 1001. (e) In (b) NOT applies only to p because it has the highest precedence; in (c) the brackets change the order so NOT applies to the result of the AND.

wpool.q: A VHDL model of an XOR gate has gate_delay = 15 ns and input a changes at t = 100 ns (0 to 1) while b = 0. (a) When does output c change? (b) A half adder built from three gates 7408, 7404, 7408 (15 ns each) has what total delay at the Sum output? (c) Why simulate the delay before manufacture?
wpool.sol: (a) c <= (a xor b) after gate_delay so c changes (0 to 1) at 100 + 15 = 115 ns. (b) 3 × 15 = 45 ns. (c) In high-speed circuits the spurious transient states caused by delay can produce unpredictable behaviour; simulation with a test bench lets you check and refine before manufacture (Tooley 17.9, 17.10).

wpool.q: A 4.7 GB film (1 GB = 10⁹ bytes) must be loaded into the IFE memory. (a) The loading time over a 100 Mbit/s link and over 1 Gbit/s (ignoring overhead). (b) If an aircraft loads 8 such films one after another over Gigabit, the total time? (c) Why does Tooley say Gigabit Ethernet is preferred?
wpool.sol: (a) $t=4.7\times8\times10^9/10^8$ = 376 s ≈ 6.3 min; at 1 Gbit/s: 37.6 s. (b) 8 × 37.6 s = 300.8 s ≈ 5.0 min. (c) Digital media files are large so the link must be very fast; 100 Mbit/s suffices but is ten times slower (Tooley 19.3).

wpool.q: The low cabin chime is a 494 Hz sine wave, the high chime 587 Hz, each lasting 900 ms. (a) The period of each tone. (b) The number of cycles in one chime. (c) State the four chime signals of Tooley's convention and where they are sent from.
wpool.sol: (a) $T_{low}=1/494$ = 2.024 ms; $T_{high}=1/587$ = 1.704 ms. (b) 494 × 0.9 = 444.6 cycles; 587 × 0.9 = 528.3 cycles. (c) Passenger call: a single high tone from seats and toilets to the cabin crew; attendant call: high/low between cabin crew stations; attendant emergency call: high/low repeated three times from the flight crew to the cabin crew; seat belt sign: a single low tone.
